title: Returning Improper Withdrawals and Transfers — Resident Trust Fund Accounts
content:
**Clause.** For the Resident Trust Fund Accounts, a withdrawal or transfer that paid for something Medicare or Medicaid covers, that lacked the required authorization, that duplicated an earlier entry or that was for the wrong amount is returned to the account within the improper charge reversal business days, for the improper part only, naming the original entry. An entry is returned once per reason.

## Reasons a return records

| Reason recorded | When it applies |
|---|---|
| payer-covered item | the entry paid for something Medicare or Medicaid covers |
| unauthorized | the entry lacked the required authorization |
| duplicate | the entry duplicated an earlier entry |
| wrong amount | the entry was for the wrong amount |

## Once per reason

The account's ledger is read before a return is recorded: an entry that already carries a return for a given reason takes no second return for that same reason. The same entry may still carry a return for a different reason.

## Hypothetical illustration

A transfer of $96.30 paid a charge of which $40.00 was for an item a payer covered. The return names that transfer, records the reason payer-covered item and returns the improper part, $40.00, not the whole $96.30.
